title: Private connectivity approval & SLA sampling PRD (brainstorm)
content:
Objective:
- Define a minimal, implementable PRD sketch for: approval gates for customer-managed connectivity (VPC/DirectConnect/VPN), audit-log schema and storage/retention, and an SLA sampling approach to validate latency/availability promises for Dedicated/Private tenants.

Context / background:
- Customers onboarding Private (VPC or on-prem) require a documented, auditable approval flow before going live. Currently we have ad-hoc Slack approvals and operations checklists; we need deterministic artifacts to feed into compliance and support.
- Audit logs today are scattered between control-plane events, infra metrics, and separate syslog exports. We need a consolidated minimal export and a lightweight sampling system to sanity-check SLAs without replaying full production traffic.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Approval gate definitions and required artifacts for each gate (network config review, egress policy, auth/KMS keys, provable audit artifacts).
- Audit event schema and tamper-evidence approach for customer-facing exports (what we send in the handover bundle).
- SLA sampling spec: how we pick probes, retention of samples, and how to represent sampled violations in reports.
- Handover checklist for Onboarding/SE/Support.
- Automation ideas for Console UI and API (can be incremental).

Out of scope (for this PRD):
- Deep storage tiering for archival >7 years (legal can drive later).
- Extremely high-frequency telemetry; we only define sampling, not full MDM.

Principles / constraints:
- Minimal risk to customer networks: approval checks must be non-invasive and read-only unless explicitly authorized.
- Audit logs must be customer-filterable and exportable in a compact, verifiable format.
- Approval gates should be automatable but allow manual override with recorded justification.
- Keep cost reasonable: sampling should provide statistical confidence with low probe overhead.

Proposal: Approval gates (three-phase model)
1) Pre-provisioning sanity check (automated)
   - Inputs: VPC CIDR, peering/bgp config, required endpoints whitelist, egress CIDR list, customer contact + maintenance window.
   - Checks: overlapping CIDRs with Redwood infra, forbidden IP ranges, advertised routes, presence of NAT/IGW for expected egress, DNS resolution to Redwood endpoints from a temporary probe (optional).
   - Output: precheck report with pass/fail and autogenerated remediation suggestions.

2) Security & policy review (semi-automated + human)
   - Inputs: IAM roles, KMS key identifiers, SSH/TLS fingerprint for edge appliances, ACLs.
   - Human step: security engineer reviews cross-account roles, KMS policies, and default-deny rules.
   - Decision: Approve / Request changes / Reject. If approved, record approver, timestamp, and supporting evidence (snapshots of policies).

3) Go-live gating (final)
   - Triggered when customer signals readiness and scheduling allows.
   - Must include: recorded approval from SE/Security, audit bundle generation, known rollback path (DNS rollback, route withdraw), and canary plan (small amount of traffic or internal-only).

Approval metadata to store per-gate (minimal fields):
- gate_id
- tenant_id
- gate_type (precheck | security | go-live)
- status (pending | approved | rejected | manual_override)
- approver (name + role)
- approved_at (ISO timestamp)
- rationale / notes (free text)
- linked_artifacts (ids or urls)
- request_id (control-plane request id)

Audit log requirements (high level):
- Single, queryable stream that joins control-plane events, approval events, and handover exports.
- Logs must support: filtering by tenant_id, by time range, and by action-type.
- Tamper-evidence: store an append-only export (object store) with periodic signed manifests. Option: lightweight hash-chain over daily export blobs signed by a Redwood key (KMS). This avoids full blockchain but provides tamper detection.
- Export formats: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) + gz for bundling.
- Minimum retention in control-plane: 1 year online, 3 years nearline (policy configurable per-customer). We will default to 1y online / 3y nearline.

Suggested minimal audit event schema (plain text canonical layout):
- event_id | timestamp_utc | tenant_id | actor | actor_type | action | resource | result | request_id | session_id | metadata
- Example: e1f3a7 | 2026-01-21T14:12:03Z | tenant-123 | marcos@redwood.com | human | approve_gate | network_gate/pg-45 | success | req-20260121-488 | sess-9f8 | {ip_probe: "10.12.8.1", diff: "cidr_overlap: false"}

Notes on Privacy / redaction:
- Audit exports destined for customers should redact internal-only fields (internal machine names, ephemeral tokens).
- Exports for compliance (SOC/ISO) can include more details but require RBAC gating and signed access requests.

Tamper-evidence mechanics (detailed idea):
- Every 24h Redwood control-plane generates a compressed ndjson blob of all events for that day.
- Compute SHA256 digest per-blob and store digest in a signed manifest item in KMS-backed signing key.
- Provide customers the manifest for days included in their handover package. Optionally, provide an independent public key fingerprint for offline verification.

SLA sampling spec (short):
Goal: surface out-of-band violations (latency P99, error spikes) between full SLO evals. Not intended as complete monitoring, but as an auditable sampling layer for handover + legal.
- Probe types: synthetic HTTP/gRPC probe, TLS handshake probe, DNS resolution probe.
- Sampling frequency: default 5 probes/minute for canary tenant during first 72 hours after go-live, then 1 probe/minute for next 7 days, then 1 probe/10min steady-state (configurable by customer).
- Probe placement: at least two vantage points: Redwood-managed probe in same region and a customer-provided probe (optional).
- Metrics captured per probe: timestamp, latency_ms, status_code, error, route_hops (where possible), probe_id, tenant_id, probe_type.
- Storage: probes are short-lived; full probe details retained for 30 days online, then sampled down to 1-in-100 for 1 year, then aggregate-only for longer retention.
- Violation reporting: sampling only flags candidate violations; when a sampled probe exceeds thresholds, mark for full SLO re-eval and tie to corresponding audit events (requests and approvals) to determine context.

Handover artifact bundle (what we give the customer at go-live):
- Signed manifest of daily audit blob digests for last N days (configurable, default 30 days).
- A filtered ndjson export of approval events for the tenant (jsonl file).
- SLA sample report for the canary window (csv + quick summary).
- Operating playbook: rollback steps, emergency contacts, maintenance windows.

Operator / Console UX ideas (incremental):
- Console tab: "Network Approvals" showing pending gates, attached artifacts, quick links to open remediation tickets (creates PRIVNET tickets).
- Approval action button supports: approve, request-changes, approve-with-conditions (auto-create follow-up checklist).
- Audit explorer: simple query builder to filter tenant_id + time range + event-type, export to ndjson.
- Handover generator: create/archive handover bundles with signed manifest and one-click download for permitted customer admins.

Rollout & implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (spike, 2 weeks): prototype daily blob manifest and signing flow + small console mock.
- Phase 1 (MVP, 6 wks): implement precheck automation, store approval metadata, generate daily audit blobs.
- Phase 2 (3 months): add security review workflow + manual approvals UI, add SLA sampling engine and short-term retention.
- Phase 3 (3–6 months): polished handover bundles, RBAC for exports, retention policy UI.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default retention policy: legal wants 7+ years for some customers; we need pricing/ops implications.
- Consent for customer-provided probes: if a customer runs probes from their network, who owns the probe telemetry? Need TOS language.
- Signed-manifest trust model: is KMS-signed manifests good enough, or do enterprise customers want an external auditor key?
- How granular should the approval metadata be (audit volume vs. usefulness)?

Edge cases / gotchas:
- Customer requests manual override but later disputes a change — need to keep full justification snapshots and link to ticket threads.
- Network flapping during canary: what is the automatic rollback threshold? (TBD)
- Cross-account KMS policies: verifying a customer KMS policy through automation is tricky; we may need an SE checklist instead of full automation.

Handover checklist (working):
- [ ] Precheck report: passed or documented exceptions
- [ ] Security review: approved by security@redwood.com
- [ ] SE approval: documented canary plan and rollback
- [ ] Signed manifest generated and stored
- [ ] Handover bundle created and link shared with customer admin
- [ ] Post-go-live SLA sampling scheduled and monitored for 72h canary

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments:
- Consider offering an "audit+retention add-on" (paid) for customers who need >3y retention; include easy pricing model by GB-month.
- Sampling confidence calculation: include suggested sample size table for P99 estimation given traffic volume.
- Could leverage object storage immutability + governance tags for additional tamper protection.

Next steps (near term):
- Run spike to produce daily blob + signed manifest (assign Marco).
- Draft customer-facing handover template and SE checklist (assign Sophie).
- Legal to propose minimal retention options and required TOS additions (reach out to Priya in Legal).

References / links (internal):
- Jira: PRIVNET-487 (onboarding approval automation)
- Confluence: Private Networking Audit Notes (design context)
- GH: private-deployments PR #291 (initial probe service)

-- end draft --

Unresolved: finalize default probe cadence and retention tiers.
__notes: Informal working doc: contains brainstorms, checklists, and open questions. Intended as a Google Drive working doc; will be refined into a formal PRD and engineering tickets if the spike is greenlit.
